{{short description|American mathematician}}
'''Susan Marie Hermiller''' is an American mathematician specializing in the [[Computational group theory|computational]], [[Combinatorial group theory|combinatorial]], and [[Geometric group theory|geometric]] theory of [[group (mathematics)|groups]]. She is a Willa Cather Professor of Mathematics and a former Graduate Chair for Mathematics at the [[University of Nebraska–Lincoln]].

==Education and career==
Hermiller earned a bachelor's degree in mathematics and physics from [[Ohio State University]] in 1984. She went to [[Cornell University]] for graduate study in mathematics, earning a master's degree in 1987 and completing her Ph.D. in 1992.{{r|cv}} Her [[doctoral advisor]] was [[Kenneth Brown (mathematician)|Kenneth Brown]], and her dissertation was ''[[Abstract rewriting system|Rewriting Systems]] for [[Coxeter group|Coxeter Groups]]''.{{r|mgp}}

After postdoctoral research at the [[Mathematical Sciences Research Institute]] and the [[University of Melbourne]], she became an assistant professor of mathematics at [[New Mexico State University]] in 1994.
She moved to the University of Nebraska–Lincoln in 1999.{{r|cv}}

In 2021, her joint research with Mark Brittenham disproved the longstanding Bernhard-Jablan conjecture in knot theory, demonstrating that a proposed algorithm for determining the unknotting number of a knot was not viable. <ref name=brittenham>{{Cite journal |last1 = Brittenham |first1 = Mark |last2 = Hermiller |first2 = Susan | year = 2021 | title = A Counterexample to the Bernhard–Jablan Unknotting Conjecture. |journal = Experimental Mathematics |volume = 30 |issue = 4 |pages = 547–556 |doi = 10.1080/10586458.2019.1580633 |arxiv = 1705.05985 | url= https://doi.org/10.1080/10586458.2019.1580633 |name-list-style=vanc}}</ref>

In 2025, the pair gave a counterexample to another long-standing conjecture, showing that the [[unknotting number]] is not additive under the [[connected sum]]. They proved that the connected sum of the [[71 knot|Septoil knot]] with its mirror image, <math>7_1 \# \overline{7_1}</math>, has unknotting number 5, although each individual knot has unknotting number 3.<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last1=Brittenham |first1=Mark |last2=Hermiller |first2=Susan |title=Unknotting number is not additive under connected sum |eprint=2506.24088 |class=math.GT |year=2025}}</ref>

==Service==
Hermiller was a founding member of the Committee on Women in Mathematics of the [[American Mathematical Society]], in 2013.{{r|cowim}} She also served as the American Mathematical Society representative on the Joint Committee on Women in the Mathematical Sciences for 2011 through 2013.{{r|jcw}} She was also a former AMS Council member at large.<ref>{{Cite web |title=AMS Committees |url=http://www.ams.org/about-us/governance/committees/mal-past.html |access-date=2023-03-27 |website=American Mathematical Society |language=en}}</ref>

==Recognition==
Hermiller became the Willa Cather Professor in 2017.{{r|6fep}}
She was included in the 2019 class of fellows of the [[American Mathematical Society]] "for contributions to combinatorial and geometric group theory and for service to the profession, particularly in support of underrepresented groups".{{r|fams}}
